items.title: Haze: Outdoor events may be moved indoors as 808 hotspots detected in Kalimantan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Organisers may need to move outdoor events indoors if air quality deteriorates amid the current haze situation, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup. He said the move was important to reduce public exposure to polluted air, particularly when Air Pollutant Index (API) readings reached unhealthy levels. He said appropriate measures would be taken based on prevailing haze conditions and API readings, in line with the Haze Action Plan and standard operating procedures.

items.title: National interests must transcend racial, religious differences, says Aaron
items.summary: National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said that in conjunction with the 63rd Malaysia Day celebration, the people are also urged to continue respecting one another, sharing common values, and preserving the unity and harmony that are the foundations of the country’s peace, stability and prosperity. From Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah and Sarawak, each community contributes to Malaysia’s unique and rich face. “Happy Malaysia Day 2026.

items.title: Wan Junaidi calls for mature, inclusive Malaysia as nation marks Malaysia Day
items.summary: The Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, said the strength of a nation is not measured solely by economic progress or physical development, but also depends on maturity and wisdom in managing its diversity. “Malaysia today is entering an era that demands new ways of thinking. Wan Junaidi said Malaysia Day also served as a reminder that true progress could only be achieved when no one was left behind in the nation’s development.

items.title: Bersatu Perlis hit by mass resignations, 114 branch chiefs quit
items.summary: ARAU: The resignation of 114 Bersatu branch chiefs in Perlis signals a deepening crisis within the party that could have wider implications, an academic said. Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) lecturer Muhammad Izmer Yusof said the development was not surprising, as Bersatu had limited strength when contesting on its own. He said past election results showed the party had relied on the strength of its coalition partners.

items.title: Putrajaya Immigration detains 173 foreign nationals at Sepang construction site
items.summary: Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 88 officers of various ranks were deployed to conduct inspections at the site. He said 261 individuals, comprising 217 foreign nationals and 44 locals, were checked during the operation. Of the total, he said 147 were Bangladeshi men, 17 Indonesian nationals and nine Pakistani nationals.

items.title: 5,000 expected at BCCK for national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebration
items.summary: KUCHING: About 5,000 people are expected to gather at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) tonight for the national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebration. Sarawak is hosting the national celebration once again, having last held the event in 2023. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor are also scheduled to attend.

items.title: Women's drug abuse cases rise by 3.3pct last year
items.summary: Ruslin said a report by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) found that women faced far more complex challenges than men in accessing treatment. "Society tends to view drug addiction among women as a greater moral failure compared with men," he said. "We also provide AADK's Borderless Rehabilitation Treatment Mobilisation (MRT) service to rural areas, helping to overcome logistical constraints often faced by women," he said.

items.title: More than 2.6 million Malaysians visited Indonesia in 2025 as neighbours gear up for 70 years of diplomatic ties
items.summary: Malaysia’s Chargé d’Affaires to Indonesia Farzamie Sarkawi said this at the Malaysia Day celebration hosted by the Embassy of Malaysia in Jakarta, here on Tuesday night, highlighting the unique relationship between the two countries, which share history, language, and culture. Farzamie said bilateral cooperation continues to gain momentum, with trade reaching US$34.22 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in 2025, while Malaysia remained Indonesia’s fourth-largest investor with investments amounting to US$4.5 billion. He said people-to-people connections also remained strong, with more than 2.63 million Malaysian tourists visiting Indonesia last year, making Malaysia the largest source of foreign visitors to the republic, while 4.26 million Indonesian tourists visited Malaysia.

items.title: Five held after obstructing enforcement team at Tasek Bera Ramsar site
items.summary: BERA: Police detained five people, including four women, for allegedly obstructing an enforcement team during a joint operation at the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve (Ramsar) yesterday. District police chief Superintendent Zulkiflee Nazir said the five allegedly obstructed and provoked enforcement personnel during the operation around 10am. He said the operation involved several enforcement agencies and was conducted under the National Forestry Act 1984.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia won’t be transit point for shipments supporting Israel’s military, suspicious cargo will be inspected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday reaffirmed Malaysia’s firm stance against allowing the country to be used as a transit point for any cargo contributing to Israel’s military operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Anwar stressed that Malaysia remains committed to preventing the country from being used to support military aggression or acts against innocent lives. “Malaysia’s position is clear and unequivocal.

items.title: Wall Street ends lower as oil spikes and the benchmark Treasury yield breaches 5pct
items.summary: NEW YORK: Wall Street extended its selloff on Tuesday, as rising US Treasury yields, mounting debt concerns and soaring crude prices kept buyers on the sidelines. All three major US stock indexes extended Monday's losses as broad risk-off sentiment weighed on nearly every sector but energy. In the wake of last week's hot inflation data and the near 25 per cent jump in US crude prices over the last two weeks, financial markets have priced in more than a 95 per cent likelihood of a rate hike on Wednesday, up from 33.1 per cent one month ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

items.title: Driver who rammed three vehicles tests positive for four drugs
items.summary: City Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the crash occurred at 3.50pm two days ago. Footage of the incident subsequently went viral on Threads, prompting traffic police to track down all the vehicles involved. He said the Honda Civic driver went to the police station to lodge a report at 10.39pm yesterday.

items.title: Japan bond yields extend gains on inflation concerns ahead of Fed decision
items.summary: Yields move inversely to bond prices. The 20-year JGB yield climbed 4 bps to 3.925 per cent. The 30-year yield added 4 bps to 4.190 per cent.

items.title: Anwar calls for Malaysia-Maldives ties to deliver tangible gains in trade, tourism and digital economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia and the Maldives have ample scope to strengthen parliamentary cooperation, including through exchange visits, sharing of experiences and the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) platform, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. During the visit, he also held several meetings with the Maldives leadership to expand cooperation in strategic areas, including education, defence, trade, investment, tourism, the halal industry and the digital economy. Anwar said his meeting with Maldives Vice-President Hussain Mohamed Latheef also discussed efforts to expand cooperation in higher education, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), professional training and human capital development.

items.title: 40 districts nationwide record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: All affected areas recording unhealthy air quality were in Peninsular Malaysia. Meanwhile, 23 districts recorded moderate air quality, mostly in Sarawak, including Kuching (75), IPD Serian (73), Samarahan (70), and Sibu (66). Sabah also recorded moderate air quality, including at Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (64), Keningau (56), and Sandakan (53).

items.title: Japan August imports jump as oil prices lift costs, exports stay firm
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's imports rose sharply for a third straight month in August as higher crude oil prices lifted energy costs, while exports rose for a 12th month in a row on resilient semiconductor-related demand, government data showed on Wednesday. Total imports by value grew 28 per cent from a year earlier in August, Ministry of Finance data showed, compared with a median market forecast for a 26.3 per cent increase, as elevated crude oil prices boosted energy imports despite the yen's spike after a rare joint yen-buying intervention with the United States. Exports by value rose 19.3 per cent year-on-year in August, compared with economists' median forecast for an 18.2 per cent increase and following a 23.2 per cent rise in July, supported by strong chip-related shipments and higher non-ferrous metal prices.

items.title: RM470bil investment target for Northern Corridor Economic Region by 2030 [WATCH]
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government has set a target for cumulative realised investment in the Northern Corridor Economic Region (NCER) to reach RM470 billion by 2030, RM126.2 billion more than the RM343.8 billion realised to date. Northern Corridor Implementation Authority (NCIA) chief executive Datuk Mohamad Haris Kader Sultan said the region is confident of achieving the target, backed by approved investments expected to materialise over the coming years. Mohamad Haris said several potential automotive investments are being assessed, although NCER has yet to determine how much the sector could contribute to the RM470 billion target.

items.title: King and Queen extend Malaysia Day greetings, pray for lasting peace and unity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, King and Queen of Malaysia, have extended Malaysia Day greetings to all Malaysians. In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, the King and Queen also prayed that Malaysia would continue to be blessed by Allah SWT, enjoy lasting peace, and remain protected from all forms of adversity. Sultan Ibrahim also expressed gratitude for the longstanding unity and harmony among Malaysians of different races, saying these are vital to the country’s strength and stability.

items.title: AGC: Dropping four charges against Muhyiddin based on evidence, litigation risks; three Jana Wibawa charges remain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) stressed that the decision not to proceed with the four charges against Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin in relation to Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd was made based on a professional assessment of the evidence, the evidential viability of the case and the overall interests of the prosecution. “In such circumstances, the prosecution must consider the overall interests of the case rather than defend one charge in isolation,” it said. The prosecution in Muhyiddin’s trial closed its case today after calling 29 prosecution witnesses.

items.title: Washington set to approve US$2.8bil arms package for Israel
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US federal government is on track to approve a US$2.8 billion arms package for Israel, US media reported Tuesday, with the sale of 40,000 one-ton bombs among the largest munitions packages sold in recent years. The New York Times said the administration of US President Donald Trump had approved the sale, citing a US official. The deal was reported amid an ongoing munitions shortage within the US military, with stocks rapidly depleting from the war with Iran and with the US spending US$22.3 billion on munitions between Feb 28 and June 30.

items.title: Diverging fortunes of Hengyuan and Petron Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two Port Dickson-based refiners are seeing sharply diverging fortunes on Bursa Malaysia, with Hengyuan Refining Co Bhd outperforming Petron Malaysia Refining & Marketing Bhd as investors weigh their ability to benefit from elevated refining margins. From end of February, when the US-Iran conflict began, Hengyuan's share price has rallied by more than 250 per cent. Since both companies reported their second-quarter (Q2) results on Aug 28, Hengyuan's share price has surged about 77 per cent to RM3.45 as at Sept 14, from RM1.95.

items.title: Malaysian firms tap Australia's multibillion-ringgit investment boom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Australia is becoming an increasingly important growth engine for Malaysian companies, as they tap billions of ringgit worth of opportunities spanning infrastructure, renewable energy (RE), mining and property. The scale of that exposure is already significant for some Bursa Malaysia-listed firms such as Gamuda Bhd, which boasts more than one-third of its RM61.6 billion outstanding order book tied to Australian construction jobs. For Sime Darby Bhd's industrial arm, the opportunities include RM21 billion of spending ahead of the 2032 Brisbane Olympics, Sydney Metro's RM60 billion investment plan over the next four years and Western Australia's aim to attract RM160 billion in private investments over four years.

items.title: PH weighs going solo in Melaka polls as seat talks with BN hit impasse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Going solo has emerged as Pakatan Harapan's most strategic option for the upcoming Melaka state polls as cooperation with Barisan Nasional has reached an impasse, political analysts said. This follows BN's firm stance to defend all 21 seats it won in the 2021 state election. The issue escalated after acting Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim said PH was ready to contest all 28 state seats independently.

items.title: Attempted Trump assassin ordered packages using Bob Dole's name, new records show
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Tuesday the FBI had discovered new information regarding the shooter who attempted to assassinate Donald Trump during a campaign event in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024. "It is new information about the shooter and about his background, about his history and that stuff that we didn't know before," Blanche told reporters during a White House press conference, declining to elaborate. A person who reviewed documents detailing the new information said it includes that the shooter had packages delivered to him under the pseudonym Bob Dole, the late Republican senator and presidential candidate.

items.title: Armed Forces maps out 5D strategy to counter future threats [WATCH]
items.summary: Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the strategy was aimed at ensuring the force remained credible and prepared to deal with threats across the land, sea, air, cyber and electromagnetic domains. He said this year's 93rd Armed Forces Day theme, "Armed Forces' Resilience, the Nation's Defence Bastion" ( Ketahanan ATM, Benteng Pertahanan Negara ), reflected the importance of resilience in enabling the force to fulfil its core responsibility of safeguarding national security and sovereignty. THE 5D STRATEGY Malek said the 5D strategy — Diplomacy, Detect, Deter, Deny and Defeat — provided the strategic approach for developing a credible "Future Force".

items.title: Cyber Force to become fourth Armed Forces service by 2030 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The armed forces have established a nucleus team to spearhead the formation of a Cyber Force, which is targeted to become operational by 2030. Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the fourth service was necessary as cyberspace and electromagnetic warfare had become critical domains in modern security and military operations, with regional neighbours and other countries already developing similar capabilities. The team will plan and assess the steps needed to turn the Cyber Force operational.

items.title: More than 100,000 Armed Forces personnel declare assets amid corruption push [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 100,904 armed forces personnel have declared their assets as the military tightens oversight of high-risk positions and strengthens safeguards against corruption and misconduct. "We have achieved 97.53 per cent, involving 100,904 officers and personnel," said Malek. "I have also redeclared my assets after being appointed armed forces chief.

items.title: South Korean workers challenging Trump administration over Georgia raid
items.summary: BARCELONA: More than 300 South Korean workers who were detained in last year's immigration raid at a Hyundai electric-vehicle manufacturing plant in Georgia are challenging the US government, CNN reported on Tuesday. US authorities arrested hundreds of workers, most of whom are South Korean nationals, in the raid at the Hyundai-LG battery project last September. "ICE Homeland Security Investigations, in coordination with our law enforcement partners, executed a judicial search warrant as part of an ongoing criminal investigation into allegations of unlawful employment practices and other serious federal crimes," a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security told Reuters on Tuesday.

items.title: Celebrating 63 years of togetherness: East Malaysians share what it means to be Malaysian
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU/KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Julia Chan and Arif Zikri spoke to Sabahans and Sarawakians on what Malaysia means to them and what it means to be Malaysian. Ahead of Malaysia Day, Malay Mail asked several Sabahans what comes to mind when they hear “Malaysia”, what being Malaysian means to them, how that identity differs in Sabah, and what they wish people in Peninsular Malaysia understood about being Sabahan. What comes to mind when you hear “Malaysia”?

items.title: US curbs S. Africa visas, alleging 'race-based discrimination'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States on Tuesday announced new restrictions on visas for South Africans, after President Donald Trump repeatedly criticised the country's leaders over its post-apartheid racial justice policies. In 2025, he berated President Cyril Ramaphosa in the Oval Office over discredited claims of a "white genocide" in South Africa. Ties between the two nations have nosedived since Trump took office last year, with the US leader cutting aid, expelling the South African ambassador and offering "refuge" to South African whites fleeing "persecution."

items.title: After Gunung Kinabalu, porter conquers Chamonix ultra-trail
items.summary: AFTER more than a year of training for one of the world's toughest ultra-trails, Gunung Kinabalu porter Daved Simpat crossed the finish line in Chamonix, France — carrying far more than just a personal achievement. "Gunung Kinabalu has shaped me and is part of my life," he told the 'New Straits Times'. At 4,095m above sea level, Gunung Kinabalu has served as Daved's workplace and training ground for most of his adult life.

items.title: Colombian president fires national statistics chief
items.summary: BOGOTA: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella fired his statistics chief after the official ruled out inconsistencies in unemployment figures under the previous government, the former director said Tuesday. De la Espriella took office in August and has accused his predecessor Gustavo Petro, Colombia's first-ever leftist leader, of corruption. The president announced the dismissal of Ricardo Valencia as head of the national statistics agency (DANE) in a statement on Monday, barely three weeks after appointing him.

items.title: Haze situation may worsen as Kalimantan hotspots rise to 808
items.summary: THE number of hotspots detected in Kalimantan has surged to 808, which may cause transboundary haze to spread in the region. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said this depended on the extent of open burning in Indonesia and wind conditions. However, it said humid conditions expected in western Sarawak this week could potentially reduce the impact of transboundary haze.

items.title: Bessent defends Trump economic policies, reveals plans to meet Chinese official
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended a range of Trump administration economic policies before lawmakers on Tuesday, from currency and bond market interventions to AI safety, disclosing plans to meet with his Chinese counterpart this weekend. Bessent told a hearing of the House Financial Services Committee that US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping would continue discussions next week on Iran and China's financial links to Teheran. Bessent told reporters rising bond yields were due to "global issues," as he headed into the hearing.

items.title: Empty seats as schools reopen in Venezuela's quake-hit Guaira
items.summary: LA GUAIRA: Schools in Venezuela's quake-scarred coastal state of La Guaira were deserted on Tuesday, a day after the start of the new school year, with many parents opting to keep children home for fear of further deadly tremors. La Guaira, home to a popular resort of the same name north of Venezuela's capital Caracas, was devastated by powerful back-to-back quakes on June 24 that left over 6,500 people dead. [[nid:1533701]] Just over 300 students have enrolled for the new school year at John Paul II Diocesan Educational Unit, one of the few schools open in the port city of La Guaira.

items.title: 'Overweight' call stays on healthcare
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Malaysia's healthcare sector could gain traction, driven by its low cost, ease of access and ability to provide personalised responses to patients. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research) cited a Boston Consulting Group (BCG) survey showing that a majority of adults polled across 15 countries in November 2025 had already used generative AI tools for health-related issues. HLIB Research said the growing use of LLMs for healthcare queries could provide a more immediate tailwind for Malaysian hospital operators, such as IHH Healthcare Bhd, Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd and KPJ Healthcare Bhd.

items.title: Former Philippines leader Duterte due in ICC courtroom to assess if fit for murder trial
items.summary: THE HAGUE: Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte is expected to appear in public for the first time on Wednesday since being transferred to the International Criminal Court 18 months ago to face murder charges related to his war on drugs. Duterte, 81, served as president from 2016 to 2022, before being charged with crimes against humanity for creating, funding and arming death squads that targeted narcotics peddlers and users. Duterte's lawyer and family did not respond to requests for comment.

items.title: Trump slams Supreme Court over 'horrible' mail-in ballot ruling
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump blasted the Supreme Court on Tuesday after it blocked his divisive plan to restrict mail-in ballots, launching a rare and blistering attack on the justices he hand-picked in his first term. "The Supreme Court has really let our Country down! Trump wrote.

items.title: US Supreme Court deals blow to Trump's mail-in voting restrictions
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court dealt a major blow Monday to President Donald Trump's attempts to restrict mail-in voting before the November midterm elections, denying his request to lift an order halting the divisive plan. His counterpart in the House, Hakeem Jeffries, said the court had blocked Trump's "diabolical scheme" to restrict mail-in ballots. Several states, including North Carolina, have already begun sending mail-in ballots to voters.

items.title: MACC officer retracts police report against Muhyiddin’s lawyer; court decides not to cite for contempt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today decided not to begin contempt of court proceedings against Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation officer Mazery Mohd Zaini, as it accepted the officer’s explanations about his MACC colleague’s police report. Earlier today, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyers had accused Mazery of contempt of court, due to his actions that led to the police report. Muhyiddin’s lawyers had pointed out that Mazery was still testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s trial, and should not have communicated with anyone including the MACC colleague who lodged the police report.

items.title: Ringgit slides against euro, yen and pound as greenback gains momentum
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which begins tonight, an analyst said. “Consequently, the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.25 per cent to 99.641 points while the 10-year US Treasury note yield surpassed the 5.00 per cent level. Other Asian currencies such as the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Singapore dollar were also weaker against the US dollar,” he told Bernama today.

items.title: SWCorp: Investigation papers on construction waste dumping from Singapore to be ready in three months
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 – The Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) is currently finalising four investigation papers on the dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian. Johor SWCorp director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said that the investigation papers are expected to be completed in three months time before being referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further action. Zainal Fitri was commenting on SWCorp’s investigation progress into the alleged dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian.

items.title: Haze: 39 areas hit unhealthy API levels as of 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — A total of 39 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today. Two areas in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Serian (171) and Samarahan (151). Meanwhile, 29 areas nationwide recorded moderate API levels.

items.title: Kelana Jaya line operations back on track after morning signal fault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Rapid KL’s Kelana Jaya Line, which was disrupted by a signalling fault this morning, has returned to normal operations and is running according to schedule. Following the incident, its operations and technical teams took immediate action to restore the affected system and conducted continuous monitoring to ensure operations returned to normal as soon as possible. “Following the action taken, operations on the Kelana Jaya Line have returned to normal, and all trains are operating according to schedule,” it said.

items.title: Muhyiddin relieved after acquittal on four charges, hopes to be freed from three remaining charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin today expressed relief after the High Court decided to acquit him on four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd. Muhyiddin expressed hope that he would also be freed of the remaining three charges that he is still facing in this trial. Muhyiddin’s lawyers had urged for Muhyiddin to be acquitted on those four charges instead.

items.title: Lawyer Haniff Khatri says decades of legal notes and 28 years of memories lost in Country Homes house fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Three decades of handwritten journals, irreplaceable legal notes, and 28 years of family memories were reduced to ash early today after a devastating fire gutted the home of prominent lawyer Mohamed Haniff Khatri Abdulla in Bandar Country Homes. The blaze, which broke out around 3am, completely consumed the upper floor of the residence, incinerating beds, clothing, home appliances, and personal archives that Haniff had accumulated over more than 30 years of legal practice, NST reported. His son, Mohamed Hamzah Khatri Mohamed Haniff, sifted through the wreckage to find a handheld gaming console on his bedroom floor, one of the few items to survive the flames.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB insists has no unilateral power over Yang Di-Pertuan Besar, but stays silent on alleged proclamation signing
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 15 — Negeri Sembilan Mentri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim insisted today that he has no unilateral power over the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir, but stopped short of confirming or denying that he signed a disputed document at the centre of a growing constitutional row. The state executive council, which Ismail chairs, said in a statement that questions over the so-called Instrument of Proclamation must be resolved strictly under the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 (UUTKNS) and the principle of constitutional monarchy, "not as a political or personal matter." The statement comes after the Undang Yang Empat — the state's four ruling chiefs — and other traditional leaders publicly alleged that Ismail signed a proclamation on August 3effecting the dethronement of Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Malaysia agrees in principle to support Maldives’ US$100m soft loan request, says Anwar
items.summary: MALE, Sept 15 — Malaysia has agreed in principle to support the Maldives’ application for a US$100 million (US$1=RM4.07) financing facility, which Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described as a form of soft loan to be implemented through both countries’ monetary authorities. Anwar said that the terms and mechanism for the facility are still being worked out by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA). “The President has written to me about the need to get our central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, to respond to the Maldivian request, precisely (from) the Maldives Monetary Authority, for this US$100 million facility.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia, Maldives to expand cooperation in maritime security, halal and haj
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that as a maritime nation, the Maldives placed particular importance on maritime cooperation, including security and training. On Islamic affairs, Anwar said the Maldives’ status as an Islamic country provided opportunities to deepen cooperation in areas including halal, dakwah, Muslim affairs, waqf and haj. “Today we witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Prosecution completes case after 29 witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The prosecution today completed its case in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's power abuse trial after calling in 29 prosecution witnesses, which means that the trial will now move on to the next stage. Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin this afternoon told the High Court that the prosecution closes its case, and that the prosecution will offer six witnesses that Muhyiddin could call in as his witnesses if he is ordered to defend himself in this case. "With that, the prosecution closes this case.

items.title: Four of seven missing anglers found safe off Sekinchan, search continues for three
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 15 — Four of the seven anglers reported missing yesterday were found safe by a local fishing boat in the waters off Sekinchan, 25 nautical miles from the coast of Sungai Besar, at about 9.50 am today. Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Abdul Muhaimin Muhammad Salleh said the four men were found floating close to one another and were in a weak condition. He said the search and rescue operation was ongoing to locate the remaining three victims, with the maritime search area expanded to 203.5 square nautical miles, while the aerial search covers 764 square nautical miles.

items.title: Babysitter pleads not guilty to exposing toddler to conditions that could have caused death
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — A babysitter pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of exposing a 13-month-old boy under her care to conditions that could have caused his death last week. Noraidah Khairuddin, 44, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Irwan Suainbon. According to the charge, Noraidah, as a person having custody of the toddler, was accused of exposing him in a manner that could have caused his death.

items.title: KL police propose KK Mart stores as safety points to boost crime prevention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The Kuala Lumpur Police propose making KK Mart convenience stores as Go-To-Safety-Point (GTSP) locations through a strategic collaboration with the company to strengthen crime monitoring and prevention efforts in the capital. “We see that KK Mart can be made a safety point for the surrounding community. Meanwhile, Fadil said that the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur IPK is the first convenience store branch in the PDRM building.

items.title: Anwar moots Malaysia-Maldives joint commission in KL this year
items.summary: MALÉ, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed convening the Malaysia-Maldives Joint Commission in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year to further advance bilateral relations between the two countries. Anwar said the Commission would be an important platform to address outstanding issues and translate the close relationship between Malaysia and the Maldives into concrete cooperation. Anwar said the Commission could also address issues affecting Maldivians in Malaysia, including students and those seeking healthcare.

items.title: Don’t rush: Home minister urges Malaysians to avoid MyKad replacement frenzy
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Sept 15 — The people have been advised not to rush to replace their MyKad when applications for the new version open on Sept 17, to avoid congestion at National Registration Department (NRD) offices. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions. “I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad.

items.title: Prosecution drops four charges against Muhyiddin, presses on with three in corruption trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today acquitted former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin of four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd's funds, as the prosecution today said it does not want to proceed with trial on those charges for now. High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin delivered her decision this afternoon on whether to only grant a DNAA or to acquit Muhyiddin on those four charges. “So with that, the court discharges and acquits the accused from those four charges only.

items.title: Ipsos poll: Malaysians prioritise jobs and homes over traditional milestones
items.summary: Specifically, 67 per cent of Malaysians identify a stable job as essential, compared to 65 per cent globally, while 60 per cent view home ownership as a key milestone, slightly above the global average of 58 per cent. Parenthood and marriage are viewed as markers of success by 47 per cent and 42 per cent of Malaysians, respectively, far outpacing global figures of 31 per cent and 25 per cent. Home ownership follows closely, cited by 64 per cent of Millennials and 55 per cent of Gen Z.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Lawyer accuses MACC officer of ‘intimidation’ over police report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad today told the High Court that a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer had allegedly attempted to intimidate and tarnish his reputation as a lawyer, based on the officer’s MACC colleague’s police report. Amer, who was cross-examining MACC officer Mazery Mohd Zaini as the 29th prosecution witness yesterday in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, said the police report had false information. Amer said the police report lodged yesterday had named him and referred to the ongoing trial, and referred to an alleged classified document that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had wanted to be included as evidence in the trial.

items.title: Police receive two reports over Negeri Sembilan MB’s alleged forced signing of royal document
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 15 — Police have received two reports concerning the Proclamation document allegedly signed under duress by Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, seeking to remove the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said following the reports lodged by the Menteri Besar, the police would classify the case to determine the appropriate direction and scope of the investigation. “I can confirm that two police reports were lodged by the Menteri Besar. It is our duty, upon receiving the reports, to classify them based on the nature and direction of the investigation.

items.title: Pesta Pulau Pinang returns, but moves to Tasek Gelugor after 50 Years at Sungai Nibong
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — Pesta Pulau Pinang will return this year for a month-long celebration starting December 1, with the event relocating to Padang Menora in Tasek Gelugor. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow confirmed that while the annual event continues as scheduled, it will be held at a more compact venue compared to its traditional site in Sungai Nibong. The state government had explored several alternative locations before the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda) offered the Tasek Gelugor site.
